subject: Clarify CCPA role boundaries & subprocessor notice timeline
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmeinc.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeinc.com, privacy@acmeinc.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify CCPA role boundaries & subprocessor notice timeline

Hi Ben,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. Two quick asks from our side before we circulate to legal: 1) Under CCPA/CPRA language you’ve used "Service Provider" in several sections — we need to confirm that this maps to the narrower CCPA definition (i.e., contractual restrictions on selling, retaining/use for limited purposes). Can Redwood confirm any operational or retention differences between your hosted offering and a generic processor designation?

2) Subprocessor notice: our procurement team needs a defined outbound notice window for any new subprocessors that will process California consumer data. The current draft says "reasonable notice" — can we get a 30-day minimum notice (email + portal update)? If not, what is Redwood’s minimum?

I’ve attached our current subprocessor table for reference. Happy to jump on a short call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Gomez
Sr. Privacy Manager — Acme Inc.
privacy@acmeinc.com

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify CCPA role boundaries & subprocessor notice timeline

Lina — thanks, got it. Looping in Priyom (legal) and Monica (account lead) to confirm the exact language. Quick notes from my side: our hosted API operates under a Service Provider model for CCPA (no selling, purpose-limited use, standard deletion/retention commitments). Operationally, we do keep aggregated telemetry for service health — that’s called out in the draft.

On notice, our standard is 14 days portal notice + email for new subprocessors. That said, for enterprise deals we can accommodate a 30-day notice window if it’s listed in the DPA/addendum. Monica — can you confirm whether this deal has the approval runway for a 30-day contractual commitment?

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 10:04 AM ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Lina — thanks, got it. Looping in Priyom (legal) and Monica (account lead)

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear asks and the subprocessor table. A couple of points from legal counsel: 1) CCPA/CPRA service provider language: we can add explicit cross-references in the addendum that "Service Provider" refers to the definition in Cal. Civ. Code §1798.140(t) and confirm contractual prohibitions on selling and use beyond specified services. We'll also add operational examples (e.g., aggregated telemetry retention limited to 90 days unless otherwise agreed).

2) Subprocessor notice window: Redwood is willing to commit to a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors that will handle California consumer personal information, provided the notice window is conditional on the customer not requiring a prior on-site audit or other gating condition. If Acme requires a stricter approval (e.g., prior written consent) instead of notice, that would be a non-standard security control and may require a carve-out or SOW.

3) Transfers/Service Provider vs. Processor: for US-state addenda we typically avoid using the EU-specific "processor"/"controller" nomenclature; however to avoid confusion we can include a short mapping table in the addendum that maps Redwood’s contractual terms to both CCPA and GDPR terminology where applicable.

I’ve attached a redline of the DPA (v3) with suggested text (attachment). If this is acceptable, Ben/Monica — please confirm so we can update the HubSpot deal and prepare the countersign version.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmeinc.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify CCPA role boundaries & subprocessor notice timeline

Lina — thanks for the patience and for the subprocessor spreadsheet. We reviewed internally with procurement and legal. Redwood can accept the 30-day minimum notice for new subprocessors that handle California consumer data; we will add the explicit CCPA cross-reference language Priyom suggested.

Two operational asks from our side to include in the addendum: a) Redwood will provide a security summary for any new subprocessors within 10 business days of notice and b) for named high-risk subprocessors (if Acme marks any in the spreadsheet), Procurement will require 14 days for a fast-track review before the processor is allowed to onboard. Both items are operational and easy to include.

If that aligns with Acme’s needs, we’ll incorporate the language and send the updated DPA + addendum link. Proposed next steps: 1) Acme confirms acceptance of the 30-day notice + the two operational asks, 2) Redwood publishes the countersigned DPA and updates the subprocessor portal.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
